A leaker with a decent track record claims that next year we may see the largest iPhone display ever.

Supply chain sources reveal that Apple is testing a new display, which could potentially be used in a brand-new iPhone, though its model name remains a mystery...

The Naming Mystery of Next Year's Flagship iPhone

2027 will mark the 20th anniversary of the iPhone, and there has long been a prevailing belief that Apple is preparing a special design for the occasion. Expectations are high that Apple will come very close to the long-term vision for iPhone design this year—a "single slab of glass".

There are rumours suggesting that Apple may launch a standalone 20th anniversary edition iPhone, in a similar vein to the iPhone X. However, more recent reports indicate that this boldly designed new device will be released directly as next year's Pro models, namely the iPhone 19 Pro and Pro Max.

A third possibility is that Apple, to mark the anniversary, will skip straight from the iPhone 18 to the iPhone 20.

The Largest iPhone Display Ever

Leaker Digital Chat Station (DCS) says that supply chain sources have revealed Apple is testing the largest iPhone display it has ever made. However, compared to the existing 6.9-inch iPhone 17 Pro Max, the increase in size is actually quite modest.

In other words, they believe Apple will position it as a 7-inch display.

DCS has no information on the purpose of this new display—assuming Apple actually follows through with it—but he speculates it may be used in next year's iPhone Pro Max, though what name that model will ultimately launch under remains unknown.

9to5Mac Commentary

Apple tests all sorts of things, and most of them never actually make it to market, so even if this display does exist as a prototype within the company's supply chain, that doesn't necessarily mean it will end up in an iPhone.

That said, if Apple's goal is to present the appearance of a single slab of glass, then being able to tout it as the largest display ever does indeed seem like a logical pairing.
